The two capture points are separate checks because taking either at the wrong moment silently breaks it -- the dispatch one after the dispatch describes a paragraph the action already changed, and the readback one after the restore describes the restore rather than the read. items.title: the product prescribes a rollback whose button it does not show -- finding 053, FIXED on shell v9, user-side reachability still unproven
items.source: finding 053; found 2026-08-16 by driving listener:click#notice-action for the first time
items.note: `recoveryFor()` returns "rollback" for any format failure whose barrier says dispatched:true, and the product toasts that prescription; but `#notice`, which carries the button, is displayed only while the session state is `recoverable-error` or `restart-required`, and EDITOR_FORMAT_POSTCONDITION_FAILED puts it in neither -- it is not in RECOVERY_ERRORS. So the user is told the document may have changed unverifiably, and is offered no way back. The error is reachable on the shipped artifact: d2-presweep records it with recovery:"rollback", dispatched:true, in both browsers. WHICH SIDE TO CHANGE IS NOW DECIDED (2026-08-16, external adjudication, verified line by line): SPEC E2-B 5.13 clause three prescribes not merely rollback but that the host ENTER `recoverable-error`, so the shell is out of spec and the page is correct. The fix goes in `NarrowEditorV2Session.action()`'s catch -- compute recoveryFor(error) and call this._blockQueue(error, "recoverable-error", "editor-recovery") before rethrowing -- which touches NOTHING in the E1-C bundle (5 files, none under editor-shell-v2/). It DOES put the E2-C shell bundle from v8 to v9, and D5 round 7 is bound to v8, so it is a planned rebinding and not a slip-in. EXECUTED 2026-08-16: shell v8 -> v9 eb76c5be…, E1-C verified still intact (E1_GO_ODT_EDITOR, failedProperties []), and the seam test goes red without the fix. What is still NOT shown is that a user can reach EDITOR_FORMAT_POSTCONDITION_FAILED through the product page: the product-path route reaches recoverable-error via MUTATION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, which blocked the queue before the fix too.

items.title: the product build never calls setAccessibilityState -- SHIPPED in the second link (d538ce0b); the datum is STILL empty under WASM, which is finding 056
items.note: `refreshEditorAccessibility()` is the only thing that calls setAccessibilityState(..., true), and its single call site sits inside `#ifdef OXSDK_EDITOR_DISCOVERY` AND `#ifndef OXSDK_FINDING_016_SELECTION_BARRIER`. The product profile defines both, so the call is compiled out and getA11yFocusedParagraph() has always returned an empty paragraph there. Found by measurement, not by reading: the first run after the v3 link reported the SAME fingerprint for every paragraph while the caret moved, and that fingerprint was the hash of the empty string. Consequence: the block-identity half of the v3 link -- the barrier comparison and the paragraph in the caret answer -- is INERT on the shipped artifact, and D-BI-2 and D-BI-3 could not have held. The four native rounds this was designed from enabled accessibility themselves, which is the tree's standing lesson (harness path vs product path) landing one level in. Fixed by calling it at document open, where every profile reaches it. SHIPPED 2026-08-17 in artifact d538ce0b: the engine now reports enabled:true, unavailable empty and paragraphFresh true -- and the focused paragraph is STILL empty, with changeCount 0. Native, same sequence, same core commit, is populated at once. That is a platform difference and it is finding 056; this item is done, the datum is not. MECHANISM ESTABLISHED same day, findings/evidence/queue-block-identity/mechanism-of-056/: the call is fine and core cannot honour it. The core build is configured --with-wasm-module=writer, which sets ENABLE_WASM_STRIP_ACCESSIBILITY, which removes 26 objects from sw/source/core/access (measured: 2 objects in the wasm build, 28 native) and makes SwEditWin::CreateAccessible() return {} -- so Window::GetAccessible() is empty and SetLOKAccessibilityState() returns at `if (!xAccessible.is())` without ever attaching a listener. The shipped artifact d538ce0b agrees: zero hits for SwAccessibleMap/Document/Paragraph, 45 for LOKDocumentFocusListener. The reporting half is in the binary, the producing half is not. setAccessibilityState returns void, which is why this was silent.

items.title: answer a click with (paragraph, offset) instead of inferring it from rectangles -- OPEN, engine-side, DESIGNED and measured 2026-08-16
items.note: REWORDED after measurement. The old wording said three ambiguities 'all reduce to the same missing datum -- which BLOCK the caret is in', and that turned out to be half right. Measured natively over three rounds: (a) there IS no block index anywhere in LOK -- the focused-paragraph payload carries content/position/start/end/listPrefixLength and nothing else, and no getCommandValues command supplies one; (b) what does exist, the paragraph's own text, is a FINGERPRINT, not an identity -- two paragraphs with the same text produce a byte-identical payload while the caret rectangle moves; (c) it settles finding 046 on the cells 046 was measured on -- but NOT in general, because the comparison is between two paragraphs' text and `empty-paragraph.odt` ends with two adjacent empty paragraphs whose text is identical -- (the dispatch paragraph read '\u2022 ' and the barrier's .uno:SelectText read '    \u2022 \nBI-AFTER-EMPTY'), and it settles the same-line-different-x case by OFFSET rather than by block; (d) it does NOT settle finding 052's residual, because x is carried on a line and dropped below it (offset 4 on the line, 7 below it, same x) so every click outside the text lands at the same offset -- a real block index would not help either, since the caret genuinely is in the last block. Every one of (a)-(d) is a NATIVE result on core 26.8; whether the shipped WASM engine reports the same offsets and refreshes the a11y payload on the same schedule is owed to a relink round and is not established here. The remedy for (d) is a different shape and comes from the reference implementation rather than from the measurement: make placing the caret a CALL THAT RETURNS (paragraph fingerprint, offset), instead of posting a click and inferring the outcome from a rectangle. Muya (MarkText's editor core) never inverts that mapping -- its cursor IS {offset, block, path} and geometry only ever goes model->pixels. Design and pre-registered predictions: research/DESIGN-2026-08-16-caret-by-block-and-offset.md. BLOCKED 2026-08-17, and NOT on a link. The paragraph datum this design consumes cannot exist in the current core build (finding 056 mechanism), and no configure flag combination in 26.8 can produce one on Emscripten (finding 057: the Make variable and the C++ macro answer to different configure inputs, and --enable-wasm-strip is forced yes for Emscripten at configure.ac:1280, overriding the command line). Unblocking this needs a configure.ac change and a CORE REBUILD, which is the user's call and the user's machine time. The editorPlaceCaretV2 half already shipped and works (38 ms / 251 ms, replacing a 30 s wait); it does not depend on the paragraph datum. Note also that a rebuild buys a TEST, not a feature: adversarial review enumerated further independent runtime conditions past attachRecursive that have never been exercised.
items.checkNote: WRITTEN 2026-08-17, waiting for the link. The old check watched for `caretBlockIndex`, a field for a datum that does not exist in LOK -- so nothing could ever have implemented it and the check was green by construction. These watch the five places the change actually lives: the engine handler, the reply type, the entry point, the EXPORT LIST (an entry point that is not exported is stripped at link time and the symbol is simply absent at run time), and both halves of the worker -- the operation and the PROJECTION, because that projection is an allowlist and adding the engine half without it is how p1-3c's itemCount came to be measured natively and reported nowhere.

items.title: the engine reports enabled:true on a core build where accessibility can never work -- a capability failure wearing the costume of data
items.note: LOK's setAccessibilityState() returns void and silently does nothing when there is no accessible object, so the engine's `enabled: true` / `unavailable: ""` only ever meant 'this call did not throw'. On the shipped build it can never mean more than that, because core was built with ENABLE_WASM_STRIP_ACCESSIBILITY. The observability the second link added asked the right question of the wrong side of the boundary: it reports what WE did, not what core accepted. Remedy is small and compile-time, no new runtime machinery: include <config_wasm_strip.h> in the engine and, when ENABLE_WASM_STRIP_ACCESSIBILITY is 1, report unavailable: "core-built-without-accessibility" instead of enabled: true. Not worth a link on its own -- ride along with the next one. Until then tools/check_core_build_provides.py is the standing guard and it is RED, which is the honest state.

items.title: the page draws the whole document as one canvas and repaints all of it per edit -- never measured past one page
items.note: layoutCanvas sizes a single canvas to the full document and renderDocument repaints it after every edit. Browsers cap canvas dimensions near 32767px, so at MAX_BACKING_WIDTH 2400 an A4 document reaches the cap somewhere around a dozen pages and rendering breaks silently and browser-dependently; below the cap the per-edit repaint cost grows with document length. 'Open a user's own file' is verified for OPENING only -- nothing has ever measured that a realistic document stays editable. The machinery for the fix is already imported: editor-session.js pulls TileScheduler from reader-shell. First step is a measurement, not a fix: add a 20-page cell and find out where it actually breaks.
items.checkNote: Absent until a long-document cell exists in the product-path runner.

items.title: finding 059: core APPLIES the parameterised inline format and reports success:false, and the engine's own predicate reads that as failure -- engine-side, needs a link
items.source: finding 059, measured on the shipped v3 artifact 2026-08-17
items.note: inlineFormatArgument() dispatches .uno:Bold with {"Bold":{"type":"boolean","value":...}} and core rejects it on the shipped WASM build; bold, italic and underline all return LOK_COMMAND_FAILED and put the session into recoverable-error. The list actions use the same parameterised mechanism and still work, so the difference is this slot's argument name or type, not parameters in general. On v2 (before the fix) bold APPLIED and merely ignored `enabled` -- which is finding 045 -- so the fix turned a wrong-direction action into no action at all. BLOCKS the next link because shipping again without resolving it ships a build whose formatting buttons cannot be used. Two candidates, both needing native measurement FIRST: withdraw inlineFormatArgument (back to v2 behaviour, on-only), or find the argument form core accepts. Mechanism deliberately not named (040/048 precedent). MECHANISM ESTABLISHED same day by native control (findings/evidence/059/native/): the parameterised .uno:Bold DOES apply -- marker typed after `value:true` comes back fo:font-weight="bold", after `value:false` comes back normal -- while reporting success:false, wasModified:true. The bare form reports success:true and leaves the text NOT bold. The .uno:DefaultBullet control behaves the same way, which is why the barrier path (which does not gate on success) kept working. So DO NOT withdraw inlineFormatArgument: the fix is correct and the defect is commandResultSucceeded() at probe_engine.cpp:1696 requiring success:true, turned into LOK_COMMAND_FAILED at :2286. Candidate predicates: wasModified, or the barrier's readback. Neither is measured yet. Also unmeasured: whether the WASM build likewise applies the command while reporting failure -- if it does, the product is telling users to roll back a change that succeeded.
items.checkNote: Absent until the engine carries a resolved form, under a name that did not exist before so the flip is visible in the diff. Deliberately NOT watching `inlineFormatArgument` itself: it is present today and present is exactly the state that is broken.

blocksRelinkSemantics: An item with blocksRelink true must be AS-DECLARED **and**, if it is declared absent, it is still outstanding work -- so P1 is not complete while it is open. Two items are deliberately false: the WASM heap field was withdrawn after measurement (2026-08-16), and the search-after-reopen wedge is an observation the product does not take today. Without this field the checker would report 'P1 complete' whenever every finished item was finished, which is the exact shape of a check that agrees with whatever it is shown.
externalAdjudication2026_08_16: fable, called as a subagent, refuted the premise that the two remaining blockers cannot be measured before the relink. Verified independently, all three claims: (1) tools/build_e2_discovery_profile.py COPIES the wasm (shutil.copy2, --wasm is an input), so a diagnostic profile can be packaged around the frozen 572035ac bytes -- no engine build, same engine; (2) the frozen wasm already serialises "readback":{"parsed": / "blockCount": / "itemCount": / "html":" and "containment":{"checked": (one occurrence each; "preBlocksObserved": zero, correct -- that is today's unlinked change); (3) all six worker patch anchors match exactly once in the FROZEN dist worker. Consequence: 3b's criterion and the containment ordering are both measurable now, for the price of a Python repackage plus browser rounds. Linking before that measurement would risk a v4, which costs the whole E2-B rerun plus E2-C D0-D5 again.

linkDecision.why: `p1Complete: True` means nothing is BLOCKING the link; it does not mean the link should happen now. Held deliberately so the newly characterised engine defect (queue-selecttext-overshoots-empty-paragraph) has a chance to ride along: it is an engine fix, so it can only ship through a link, and linking today would make it cost a second one.
